# parts

Making part types: a part's bodies, connectors and parameters.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`parts.part`](#partspart): Start one size of a custom part (equipment, a fixture, a device): declare optional `hosting` (`"wall_face"` snaps flush onto walls and auto-rotates, `"ceiling"`, `"floor"`, `"free"`), add bodies, connectors and annotative plan symbols, then build().
- [`parts.faces`](#partsfaces): The faces a connector can go on: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.
- [`parts.rect`](#partsrect): A rectangle profile (width along the view's first axis, height along its second), centred unless center moves it; corners filleted or chamfered.
- [`parts.circle`](#partscircle): A circle profile of a diameter, centred unless center moves it.
- [`parts.polygon`](#partspolygon): Any closed polygon profile of fixed corners (wound either way); corners filleted or chamfered.
- [`parts.views`](#partsviews): The views a profile is drawn in: plan (x right, y up; bodies go up), front (y right, z up; bodies go toward the front, +x), side (x right, z up; bodies go left, +y).
- [`parts.starterTypes`](#partsstartertypes): The starter library's part types in every discipline, filtered by words in the family, type, category or id.
- [`parts.refreshBuiltins`](#partsrefreshbuiltins): Upgrades stale built-in part types already pinned in an existing model to the latest library symbols (`mode: "symbols"`, default) or full definitions (`mode: "full"`) as one atomic edit, leaving placed parts and custom types untouched.

## parts.part

Start one size of a custom part (equipment, a fixture, a device): declare optional `hosting` (`"wall_face"` snaps flush onto walls and auto-rotates, `"ceiling"`, `"floor"`, `"free"`), add bodies, connectors and annotative plan symbols, then build().

```ts
part(name: string, start: { type: string; category: PartCategory; description?: string; hosting?: "free" | "wall_face" | "ceiling" | "floor"; tagFields?: string[] }): PartBuilder
```

Topics: custom part, equipment, rooftop unit, rtu, water heater, panel, family, wall_face, hosting

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.faces

The faces a connector can go on: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.

```ts
faces: readonly ("top" | "bottom" | "front" | "back" | "left" | "right")[]
```

Topics: face, connector, side

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Box", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.box({ length: v.width, width: units.in(12), height: units.in(12) });
    for (const face of parts.faces) if (face === "top") b.connector(face, { id: "out", label: "Outlet", domain: "duct", systemKind: "supply_air", shape: "round", diameter: units.in(10), endType: "mechanical.slip" });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.box.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.rect

A rectangle profile (width along the view's first axis, height along its second), centred unless center moves it; corners filleted or chamfered.

```ts
rect(width: Length, height: Length, opts?: { center?: [Length, Length]; fillet?: Length; chamfer?: Length }): Profile
```

Topics: profile, rectangle, rounded corners, fillet, chamfer

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Cabinet", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    b.extrude(parts.rect(v.width, units.in(18), { fillet: units.in(1) }), { to: units.in(30) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.cab.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.polygon

Any closed polygon profile of fixed corners (wound either way); corners filleted or chamfered. Use for curbs, hoods, brackets, odd housings.

```ts
polygon(points: [Length, Length][], opts?: { fillet?: Length; chamfer?: Length }): Profile
```

Topics: profile, polygon, outline, custom shape, hood

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Hood", { type: "48", category: "mechanical_equipment" });
    b.extrude(parts.polygon([[units.in(0), units.in(0)], [units.in(48), units.in(0)], [units.in(48), units.in(24)], [units.in(12), units.in(36)], [units.in(0), units.in(36)]], { chamfer: units.in(2) }), { on: "side", from: units.in(-12), to: units.in(12) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.hood.48", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.views

The views a profile is drawn in: plan (x right, y up; bodies go up), front (y right, z up; bodies go toward the front, +x), side (x right, z up; bodies go left, +y).

```ts
views: readonly ("plan" | "front" | "side")[]
```

Topics: view, plane, orientation, which way

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "part",
  reads: {},
  parameters: { width: { type: "quantity", kind: "length", unit: "in", label: "Width", default: units.in(24) } },
  run(ctx, v) {
    const b = parts.part("Plate", { type: "24", category: "generic" });
    for (const view of parts.views) if (view === "front") b.extrude(parts.rect(v.width, units.in(12)), { on: view, to: units.in(0.5) });
    ctx.parts.define("acme.plate.24", b.build());
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.starterTypes

The starter library's part types in every discipline, filtered by words in the family, type, category or id. Place one with equipment.place by its id (the type is pinned into the model with the placement).

```ts
starterTypes(ctx: ScriptContext, words?: string): readonly StarterType[]
```

Topics: starter library, part types, built-in parts, catalogue, panelboard, receptacle type

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const panel = parts.starterTypes(ctx, "panelboard")[0];
    if (!panel) throw new Error("No starter panelboard");
    equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: panel.id, at: { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(1) }, mark: "LP-1" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## parts.refreshBuiltins

Upgrades stale built-in part types already pinned in an existing model to the latest library symbols (`mode: "symbols"`, default) or full definitions (`mode: "full"`) as one atomic edit, leaving placed parts and custom types untouched.

```ts
refreshBuiltins(ctx: ScriptContext, opts?: { typeIds?: readonly string[]; mode?: "symbols" | "full" }): readonly { typeId: string; familyName: string; typeName: string }[]
```

Topics: refresh symbols, upgrade part types, built-in symbols, annotative symbols, stale symbols, refreshBuiltins

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const updated = parts.refreshBuiltins(ctx);
    ctx.report("refreshed", updated.length);
  },
});
```

</details>
